key_insight: Boltz-Flow improves robot action generation by replacing fixed Gaussian initialization with an observation- and instruction-conditioned Boltzmann source while keeping the base vision-language-action policy unchanged.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can improve flow-based robot policies by adapting their initialization to task context rather than redesigning the action-generation backbone.
method: Assign energies to binary source states using a conditional Boltzmann machine.
Train with an offline-demonstration-based listwise objective that aligns source energy with action quality after frozen flow integration.
At inference, solve the resulting Ising instance, decode it into continuous noise, and run one standard flow integration.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmarks, Boltz-Flow improves π₀.₅, outperforms compared policy and noise-optimization baselines on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0, and ranks second to LEAP on LIBERO-Plus; additional tests show gains with SmolVLA and other adaptation settings.
watch_item: Training uses a physical coherent Ising machine, and the abstract does not quantify solver overhead or deployment latency.
paper_title: Boltz-Flow: Generating High-Quality Robot Action from Boltzmann Machine
